Title: Credit card fraud detection and concept-drift adaptation with delayed supervised information
Problem_Dataset: Real industrial card datasets (concept drift & imbalanced streams)
Graph_Model_Method: Tabular ensemble classifiers (Random Forest, separate feedback vs delayed models)
Time_Treatment: Sliding/rolling daily windows with explicit concept drift
Label_Delay_Treatment: Explicitly models verification latency (delta days delay) + immediate alert-feedback interaction
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Focuses on tabular features; does not model relational graph topology or message passing
Relevance_Relationship: Foundational formulation of verification latency and alert-feedback split; non-graph

Title: Credit Card Fraud Detection: A Realistic Modeling and a Novel Learning Strategy
Graph_Model_Method: Separate feedback and delayed classifiers with aggregation/windowing
Time_Treatment: Realistic streaming timeline separating transaction time, alert feedback, and delayed chargeback maturity
Label_Delay_Treatment: Distinguishes immediate investigator feedback on top-k alerts from delayed customer reports
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Requires observed feedback/delay timestamps from proprietary bank logs; tabular only
Relevance_Relationship: Establishes realistic operational card-fraud evaluation and verification latency; baseline paradigm for our graph extension

Title: IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection Competition Dataset
Problem_Dataset: E-commerce payment transactions (590,540 train rows, 394 features; train_transaction + train_identity)
Graph_Model_Method: Benchmark dataset (tabular + entity proxies card1-card6, addr1-2, P/R_emaildomain, DeviceInfo)
Time_Treatment: TransactionDT is a relative timedelta (min=86,400) from an undisclosed reference datetime
Label_Delay_Treatment: Supplies final static binary isFraud labels (3.50% positive); no label-arrival timestamps
Evaluation_Split_Protocol: Competition train/test split by time; offline researchers must construct rolling splits
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Undisclosed calendar reference, masked V/C/D/M columns, partial identity coverage (~24.4%), no observed chargeback arrival timestamps
Relevance_Relationship: Primary public real-world benchmark specified in execution plan

Title: Enhancing Graph Neural Network-based Fraud Detectors against Camouflaged Fraudsters (CARE-GNN)
Problem_Dataset: YelpChi review fraud and Amazon product review fraud
Graph_Model_Method: Camouflage-resistant GNN with label-aware similarity measure and RL neighbor selector
Time_Treatment: Static multi-relation graph; no temporal ordering or causal edge constraints
Label_Delay_Treatment: Immediate static labels assumed for all training nodes
Evaluation_Split_Protocol: Random train/val/test node splits on static full graph (transductive)
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Static graph assumption; transductive exposure to full topology; review/social domains rather than temporal card streams
Relevance_Relationship: Seminal domain GNN baseline (B4); illustrates static transductive protocol lacking temporal causality and label maturity

Title: Pick and Choose: A GNN-based Imbalanced Learning Approach for Fraud Detection (PC-GNN)
Graph_Model_Method: Imbalance-aware GNN using node sampler (Pick) and neighborhood label-balanced sampler (Choose)
Label_Delay_Treatment: Immediate static labels; uses training labels to guide neighborhood sampling
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Does not enforce temporal edge causality or account for unreported/immature fraud labels during training
Relevance_Relationship: Representative imbalance-aware GNN baseline; shows how label-guided sampling assumes mature labels

Title: xFraud: Explainable Fraud Transaction Detection
Problem_Dataset: Large-scale e-commerce transaction graphs (up to 1.1B nodes, 3.7B edges)
Graph_Model_Method: Heterogeneous GNN detector (self-attention + message passing) paired with GNNExplainer hybrid
Time_Treatment: Temporal batch splits on industrial transaction logs
Label_Delay_Treatment: Treats training labels as fixed binary outcomes at snapshot creation; no explicit posterior for immature rows
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Proprietary industrial e-commerce platform data; does not isolate topology vs label-maturity leakage on public card benchmarks
Relevance_Relationship: Demonstrates heterogeneous transaction GNN scalability and explainability

Title: The Importance of Future Information in Credit Card Fraud Detection
Problem_Dataset: Real-world dataset (>30M transactions) and sequential card histories
Graph_Model_Method: Bidirectional LSTM using past and subsequent transactions for posterior review
Time_Treatment: Explicitly distinguishes real-time authorization (past only) from posterior detection (using subsequent card events)
Label_Delay_Treatment: Reports empirical compromised-card blocking delay profile (~1% within 1h, ~30% within 1 day, tail up to weeks)
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Posterior Bi-LSTM intentionally uses future card transactions for offline review, which is invalid for real-time authorization scoring
Relevance_Relationship: Provides the empirical compromised-card blocking latency profile that inspires our D2 delay scenario; highlights why real-time scoring must exclude future events

Title: Reproducible Machine Learning for Credit Card Fraud Detection: Practical Handbook
Venue_Status: Université Libre de Bruxelles / Online Handbook & Open Repository
Problem_Dataset: Synthetic Customer-Terminal Transaction Simulator (3 fraud scenarios) + ULB benchmark
Graph_Model_Method: Decision Trees, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Deep Learning
Time_Treatment: Explicitly enforces chronological train/validation/test splits with delay barrier (e.g., 7-day gap)
Label_Delay_Treatment: Models a fixed 7-day verification delay barrier between train and test windows
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Explicitly warns that the 3-scenario simulator is a simplified approximation of real payment-card dynamics
Relevance_Relationship: Provides our controlled mechanism simulator (Step 10-11) and prequential evaluation foundation

Title: Inductive Graph Representation Learning for Fraud Detection
Problem_Dataset: Credit card transaction datasets (real industrial & synthetic)
Graph_Model_Method: Inductive GraphSAGE and fraud-node-augmented graph representation learning
Time_Treatment: Inductive temporal evaluation appending new transactions to historical graph
Label_Delay_Treatment: Assumes training set fraud labels are immediately known or uses fixed historical cutoffs without survival-based posterior soft targets
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Does not formalize continuous label-delay survival functions S(a) or compare V0/V1/V2 maturity rules against causal neighbor-aggregate trees
Relevance_Relationship: Closest prior study in Decision Support Systems on inductive graph learning for card fraud

Title: Semi-supervised Credit Card Fraud Detection via Attribute-Driven Graph Representation (GTAN)
Problem_Dataset: YelpChi, Amazon, and FFSD (Financial Fraud Semi-supervised Dataset)
Graph_Model_Method: Gated Temporal Attention Network (GTAN) passing attribute and risk embeddings across temporal transaction graphs
Time_Treatment: Temporal transaction graph edges ordered by time bins
Label_Delay_Treatment: Propagates known labels as risk attributes; treats unlabeled nodes as semi-supervised targets rather than modeling age-dependent censoring S(a)
Evaluation_Split_Protocol: Semi-supervised splits with varying labeled ratios
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Risk propagation assumes observed labels are clean and static; does not audit future-edge leakage via static shared entities or delayed reporting bias
Relevance_Relationship: Key domain temporal GNN comparator (R15); highlights risk-label propagation without label-maturity survival modeling

Title: GADBench: Revisiting and Benchmarking Supervised Graph Anomaly Detection
Problem_Dataset: 10 supervised graph anomaly datasets (Weibo, Reddit, Tolokers, Questions, Elliptic, DGraphFin, T-Finance, etc.)
Graph_Model_Method: Benchmarks 29 models including XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost with neighbor aggregation vs GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, CARE-GNN, PC-GNN, BWGNN, GHRN
Time_Treatment: Primarily static graphs (except Elliptic/DGraphFin); random or predefined splits
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Static graph formulation; does not test rolling temporal causality or delayed label maturity
Relevance_Relationship: Crucial empirical baseline finding: boosted trees + simple 1-2 hop neighbor aggregation frequently match or outperform specialized GAD GNNs

Title: Graph Neural Networks for Financial Fraud Detection: A Review
Problem_Dataset: Comprehensive survey across card fraud, e-commerce, AML, insurance, and securities fraud
Graph_Model_Method: Taxonomy of homogeneous, heterogeneous, dynamic/temporal, and camouflage-resistant GNNs
Time_Treatment: Reviews static snapshots vs continuous-time dynamic graphs
Label_Delay_Treatment: Notes label scarcity and semi-supervised learning, but identifies realistic operational feedback delays in dynamic graphs as an open challenge
Reported_Metrics: Reviews AUC, F1, AP, Top-k Recall
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Broad survey; does not provide an empirical protocol separating topology leakage from label-maturity censoring
Relevance_Relationship: Authoritative 2025 taxonomy confirming the gap between static/semi-supervised GNN benchmarks and operational delayed-feedback constraints

Title: Data Leakage and Deceptive Performance: A Critical Examination of Credit Card Fraud Detection Methodologies
Problem_Dataset: Credit card fraud benchmarks (ULB, IEEE-CIS, synthetic datasets)
Graph_Model_Method: Audits preprocessing, SMOTE oversampling before splitting, random k-fold CV, and full-dataset normalization
Time_Treatment: Demonstrates severe metric inflation when chronological ordering is violated
Label_Delay_Treatment: Focuses on split/resampling leakage rather than continuous label-arrival survival or graph topology leakage
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Focuses on tabular pipelines and resampling leakage; does not evaluate message-passing topology leakage or Bayesian soft targets for delayed labels
Relevance_Relationship: Directly supports our strict pre-split isolation, ban on pre-split SMOTE, and time-safe normalization rules

Title: Leakage Safe Graph Features for Interpretable Fraud Detection in Temporal Transaction Networks
Problem_Dataset: Elliptic Bitcoin dataset (203,769 nodes, 234,355 edges, 49 timesteps)
Graph_Model_Method: Random Forest augmented with causal (past-only) vs static full-graph structural descriptors (degree, PageRank, HITS, k-core)
Time_Treatment: Strict temporal split (train steps 1-34, test 35-49) with causal edge visibility up to timestep t
Label_Delay_Treatment: Assumes known labels at each historical step; does not model reporting delay survival S(a) or maturity-aware training objectives
Evaluation_Split_Protocol: Causal temporal graph feature extraction vs look-ahead static graph
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Preprint; evaluated on Bitcoin Elliptic rather than multi-entity card-proxy graphs under verification latency
Relevance_Relationship: Demonstrates causal graph feature extraction and probability calibration for tree models (aligns with our B1/B2 baselines)

Title: When Graph Structure Becomes a Liability: A Critical Re-Evaluation of Graph Neural Networks for Bitcoin Fraud Detection under Temporal Distribution Shift
Graph_Model_Method: GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT, EvolveGCN vs Random Forest under seed-matched transductive vs strict-inductive protocols
Time_Treatment: Isolates training-time exposure to test-period adjacency and temporal distribution shift
Label_Delay_Treatment: No label-delay or maturity-window modeling; uses static Elliptic labels
Evaluation_Split_Protocol: Crossed transductive vs strict-inductive protocol + edge-shuffle ablation
Reported_Metrics: Illicit F1 (RF=0.821 vs GraphSAGE=0.689 under inductive; 39.5-pt F1 drop from transductive exposure)
Authors_Stated_Limitations: Single-author preprint on Bitcoin transaction flows (Elliptic), not payment-card entity graphs; does not address verification latency
Relevance_Relationship: Directly motivates our two-axis P0-P3 leakage matrix separating future topology visibility from label visibility
